headline: According to the New York Times, the Trump administration is seeking to develop a centralized master list of U.S. foreign intelligence targets including suspected foreign spies and potential intelligence recruits. The proposal stems from National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7), which directs intelligence agencies to better identify, integrate, and share information on national security threat actors. The proposal has reportedly faced resistance from the FBI and CIA. Critics warn that concentrating the identities of covert targets and potential assets in a single repository could create an unprecedented counterintelligence risk if compromised or improperly accessed. The effort reportedly began under former Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard. Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/29/us/trump-intelligence-agencies-spies-master-list.html

headline: Trump told G7 leaders he is disappointed with Putin and may drop the so-called "Anchorage agreements," Forbes Ukraine reports. After their August 2025 meeting in Alaska, Washington was reportedly ready to let Russia take all of Donetsk region as part of a peace deal. Russia claims the US violated the "spirit of Anchorage." Putin aide Ushakov, Foreign Minister Lavrov and deputy Ryabkov said Moscow expected Washington to back its claim on Donetsk after the Alaska talks. US Secretary of State Rubio denied any agreement existed: "The sides only exchanged proposals but reached no deals. Otherwise the war would already be over." Trump discussed increasing pressure on Russia at the G7 summit, though other G7 leaders are skeptical he will actually follow through, one Axios source said. @mylovanov
